svg.text: Breaking the route from faeces to mouth
Every diarrhoea control measure is a barrier placed somewhere on this road.
Faeces
Fingers
Flies
Fluids
Fields
Food
Mouth
The barriers, in order of how much they achieve
1. A latrine used by everyone in the house
2. Handwashing with soap at the two moments:
after the toilet, and before touching food
3. Safe water — protected source, covered
storage, a ladle rather than a dipped cup
4. Food covered, and reheated thoroughly
5. Refuse and standing water cleared
Numbers worth carrying
Free chlorine residual, routine ......... 0.2 to 0.5 mg/L
During an outbreak, at the point of use .. 0.5 mg/L or above
Household treatment: boil, chlorinate, or filter
Latrine sited well away from and downhill
of any well or borehole
A borehole that is never maintained becomes the
source of the next outbreak.
Why building latrines usually fails, and what works instead
Giving a household a latrine it did not ask for produces a store room. Community-led total sanitation works
because the community itself examines the problem, decides it is unacceptable, and builds with its own hands.
Change the community's decision, not the individual's habit. The unit of change is the whole village.
One household still practising open defecation keeps the risk in place for everyone else.
